three_changes_all_needed: InfoNCE instead of triplet margin: triplet has zero gradient once the margin is met, so the encoder stops as soon as it has just enough dimensions
AdaptiveAvgPool2d(2) instead of (1): global average pooling turned each patch into 64 channel means before the embedding was formed, and this cost more dimensions than the loss did

TRACK groups instead of place-in-adjacent-frames: my first retrain used groups averaging 1.2 members, so InfoNCE had almost no positives in a batch and collapsed to 1.69. coherence.tracks was already in the organ and gives ~12 per group.
open: Coverage fell 49.4% -> 25.6%. The abstention threshold (min_cosine 0.78) was calibrated on the old 6-dimensional space; a wider space puts fewer patches that close to any centroid, so it needs recalibrating rather than the space being worse.

correction.what_was_wrong: effective_dims 19.44 and naming_precision 1.000 were measured on patches drawn from ep441/443/444/446 -- the episodes the retrain trained on. A track supplies a dozen views of one object, so an anchor and a test patch can be two views of the same car. That is in-distribution scoring, not a holdout.

measured_on_holdout.note: 4.14 of the 19.44 survives leaving town; the rest was track-specific variation memorised.

correction.coverage_question_answered: The coverage drop was NOT the fixed 0.78 threshold being wrong for a wider space, which is what I predicted. The calibrated cut came out at 0.98, ABOVE 0.78, not below it.
correction.conformal_gate_is_not_at_fault: Under an exchangeable split both encoders hold their promise (every violation <= 0.007, i.e. noise). Under calibrate-here-deploy-there the current encoder blows past it (0.257 achieved against 0.10 promised). What breaks the certificate is the town changing, not the arithmetic.
